subject: Copywriting
title: The Price Ending Effect
description: A 60-second lesson on The Price Ending Effect.

hook.text: $9.99 outsells $10.00 even though the difference is one cent. The left digit anchors the perceived price.

buildup.text: MIT tested identical items at $34, $39, and $44. The $39 item sold the most. Nines signal 'deal.'

discovery.text: Luxury brands avoid .99 pricing. Chanel charges $5,000, not $4,999. Round numbers signal quality, not bargains.

twist.text: Charm pricing works less on informed buyers. When people research heavily, the penny trick loses its power.

climax.text: Price copy isn't just the number—it's how the number is displayed. Font size, color, and placement all matter.

quiz.question: Why do luxury brands avoid .99 pricing?

details.summary: Prices ending in .99 or .97 consistently outperform round numbers in sales tests. The 'left-digit effect' means $9.99 is psychologically perceived as $9, not $10. This tiny psychological trick has generated billions in additional revenue across every retail category.
details.whyItMatters: Price endings are one of the most tested and proven micro-persuasion techniques in marketing. Understanding why they work helps copywriters optimize pricing presentation for maximum conversion.
takeaways: The left digit dominates price perception — $9.99 feels like $9, not $10
Charm pricing (.99) works for value products; round numbers work for luxury
Prices ending in 7 are perceived as more trustworthy in digital marketing

faq.question: Why do prices ending in .99 work?
faq.answer: The brain processes prices left-to-right and anchors on the first digit. $7.99 anchors at '7 dollars' not '8 dollars.' This one-cent difference creates a disproportionate perception of savings. The effect is strongest when the left digit changes ($3.00 vs $2.99).

faq.question: When should you use round prices instead?
faq.answer: For luxury and premium products. Research shows round prices ($100 vs $99.99) feel more fluent and are associated with quality. Charm pricing signals bargain; round pricing signals premium. Match the price format to the brand positioning.
